short: Monarch whose intellectual pursuits and conversion to Catholicism led to her controversial abdication.
full:
Queen Christina inherited the Swedish throne at age six following her father Gustavus Adolphus's death in 1632, assuming personal rule in 1644. Highly educated and fiercely independent, she attracted prominent philosophers and artists to Stockholm, transforming the court into a center of European learning.

Increasingly averse to marriage and the duties of governance, and secretly drawn to Catholicism—which was strictly outlawed in Lutheran Sweden—she abdicated the throne in June 1654 in favor of her cousin, Charles X Gustav. She subsequently moved to Rome, where she spent the rest of her life as a prominent patron of the arts and a significant figure in the Catholic Counter-Reformation.
